question.:question/problem:
There are currently $102$ koalas living in a secluded forest, but their population is decreasing at a continuously compounded rate of $9.5 \mathrm{\% }$ per year. How many years must pass for there to be only $10$ koalas left in that forest? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The continuously compounded growth equation is $P=P_0e^{rt}$. Here $P_0=102$, $P=10$, and $r=-0.095$ per year. Solve for $t$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
10 &= 102e^{-0.095t} \\
e^{-0.095t} &= \frac{10}{102} \\
-0.095t &= \ln\left(\frac{10}{102}\right) \\
t &= \frac{\ln(10/102)}{-0.095} \\
&\approx 24.4462.
\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding to the nearest integer gives $24$ years.

question.:question/problem:
In a biology class, the teacher began the experiment with $10$ bacteria in a petri dish. After $14$ minutes, the number of bacteria increased to $781$. What was the continuously compounded growth rate of the bacteria? Round your answer to the nearest percent.

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The continuously compounded growth equation is $P=P_0e^{rt}$. Here $P_0=10$, $P=781$, and $t=14$ minutes. Solve for $r$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
781 &= 10e^{14r} \\
e^{14r} &= \frac{781}{10} \\
14r &= \ln\left(\frac{781}{10}\right) \\
r &= \frac{\ln(781/10)}{14} \\
&\approx 0.311285.
\end{aligned}
$$

The percentage rate is approximately $31.1285\%$ per minute. Rounding to the nearest percent gives $31\%$ per minute.

question.:question/worked-solution:
The continuously compounded growth equation is $P=P_0e^{rt}$. Here $P_0=4120$, $r=-0.0381$ per year, and $t=2016-2009=7$ years. Substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
A forex trader realizes that her annual profits have been growing continuously at a rate of $15 \mathrm{\% }$ per year. If she currently has a profit of $\$16700$ this year, what was her profit $5$ years ago? Round your answer to the nearest dollar.

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The continuously compounded growth equation is $P=P_0e^{rt}$. Here $P=16700$, $r=0.15$ per year, and $t=5$ years. Solve for the earlier profit $P_0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
16700 &= P_0e^{(0.15)(5)} \\
P_0 &= \frac{16700}{e^{0.75}} \\
&\approx 7888.5214.
\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding to the nearest dollar, the profit five years ago was $\$7889$.

&= 8990(0.6866023\ldots) \\
&\approx 6173
\end{aligned}
$$

According to this model, approximately $6173$ crimes occurred in $2022$.

question.:question/problem:
In a biology class, the teacher began the experiment with $14$ bacteria in a petri dish. After $6$ minutes, the number of bacteria increased to $471$. What was the continuously compounded growth rate of the bacteria? Round your answer to the nearest percent.

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The initial population is $P_0=14$, the final population is $P=471$, and the elapsed time is $t=6$ minutes. The decimal rate $r$ is per minute.

Use the continuously compounded growth equation, isolate the exponential, take natural logarithms, and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}
P &= P_0e^{rt} \\
471 &= 14e^{6r} \\
e^{6r} &= \frac{471}{14} \\
\ln\left(e^{6r}\right) &= \ln\left(\frac{471}{14}\right) \\
6r &= \ln\left(\frac{471}{14}\right) \\
r &= \frac{\ln\left(\frac{471}{14}\right)}{6} \\
r &\approx 0.5859668 \\
100r &\approx 58.59668
\end{aligned}
$$

Converting the decimal rate to a percentage and rounding to the nearest percent gives approximately $59\%$ per minute.

question.:question/problem:
There are currently $592$ koalas living in a secluded forest, but their population is decreasing at a continuously compounded rate of $4.3\%$ per year. How many years must pass for there to be only $40$ koalas left in that forest? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The initial population is $P_0=592$ and the final population is $P=40$. A decrease of $4.3\%$ per year means $r=-0.043$, with $t$ in years.

Use the continuously compounded growth equation, isolate the exponential, take natural logarithms, and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}
P &= P_0e^{rt} \\
40 &= 592e^{-0.043t} \\
e^{-0.043t} &= \frac{40}{592} \\
\ln\left(e^{-0.043t}\right) &= \ln\left(\frac{40}{592}\right) \\
-0.043t &= \ln\left(\frac{40}{592}\right) \\
t &= \frac{\ln\left(\frac{40}{592}\right)}{-0.043} \\
t &\approx 62.66575 \\
t &\approx 63\text{ years}
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the time is approximately $63$ years.
